title: contractive-headroom-controller-and-soft-throttle-for-dedicated-fleets
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: customers running Dedicated fleets report uneven latency during multi-tenant spikes and we observe headroom oscillation when multiple tenants aggressively warm burst capacity. This PR introduces a Contractive Headroom Controller (CHC) and a Soft Throttle policy to stabilize fleet-level headroom while preserving short-lived burst responsiveness.

Summary of changes: add a new controller that maintains a decaying headroom watermark per fleet, implement a tenant-facing soft-throttle that signals clients to back-off probabilistically when headroom dips below percentile thresholds, extend the telemetry pipeline with p50/p95/p99 headroom and per-tenant utilization deltas, and add e2e integration tests + canary rollout hooks.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-1842) linked in PR. 
- [x] Controller + reconciliation loop implemented. 
- [x] Backwards-compatible config knobs and operator flags. 
- [x] Observability: new metrics + dashboards. 
- [x] Unit + integration tests. 
- [x] Gradual rollout plan annotated in README.

Behavior and rationale: CHC keeps an exponentially decayed reservoir of recent free capacity that favors recent stability (lambda tunable). Instead of hard eviction, the Soft Throttle issues weighted rejections (HTTP 429 with Retry-After hints and a probabilistic Accept decision) for lower-priority tenants when fleet headroom percentile crosses configured thresholds. This reduces synchronized warmups and avoids large preemptions that hurt p99 tail latency. The design targets three SLOs: preserve median throughput, cap p99 latency regressions, and bound short-term SLA violations per tenant.

Compatibility and rollout: feature is disabled by default. Operators can enable CHC per-cluster and configure decay window, minimum headroom fraction, and throttle curves. We added a canary controller that can be bound to a single fleet and a toggle to run the Soft Throttle in simulation mode (emit telemetry decisions without applying throttles). The PR includes a migration script to backfill fleet headroom history from the last 48h of utilization samples if available.

Testing and validation: unit tests for controller reconciliation and throttle decision logic, integration harness runs simulated multi-tenant spikes to assert p99 improvements, and a short smoke test for the HTTP hinting path. Canary run on internal staging fleet for 72h showed: p99 latency -18% under modeled spike, average tenant short-term retry rate < 3%, and 2% change in overall throughput.

Operational notes: added three new Grafana panels (fleet_headroom_percentiles, tenant_util_delta, soft_throttle_reject_rate), a Prometheus rule for alerting when headroom decays below safety watermark for >5m, and an automated incident playbook entry describing rollback steps.

Related: complements prior autoscaling work (ENG-1682) and the burst-token pool refactor (PR referenced in linked Linear items).

review_comments: Bryan Cho: Can we make the decay lambda a per-fleet override? I think some clusters need faster decay. (addressed)
Marta Gómez: The probabilistic accept algorithm needs an upper bound to prevent starvation; suggest additive smoothing. (updated decision.go with smoothing)
Elliot Shaw: Add a migration fallback if historical samples are missing; otherwise headroom computes to zero. (added backfill script)
CI: test/integration failed initially due to race in reconcile; fixed by adding a reconciliation lock in controller.go
release_notes: Introduce Contractive Headroom Controller and Soft Throttle: opt-in stabilization for Dedicated fleets that reduces p99 latency during bursts and provides configurable probabilistic throttling. New metrics and dashboards added. Disabled by default; see docs/operational/headroom_controller.md for rollout instructions.
notes_on_testing: Simulated 72h canary on internal staging fleet with injected tenant spike patterns; integration harness asserts p50/p95/p99 headroom behavior and throttle fairness. Load test scripts included in internal/testing and can be replayed against staging.
post_merge_actions: Apply Helm value changes to staging via deploy/helm/values.headroom.yaml, enable canary on fleet 'staging-west-3' for 72h, monitor grafana panels, and bump telemetry retention if data is noisy.
